title: DC-area forecast: Rain chances with a flood risk tonight. Clearing, warmer Sunday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Mostly cloudy this evening with temperatures in the 70s. Shower chances increase this evening, mainly after 7 or 8 p.m., with spotty heavy rain—even a few flooding downpours possible—overnight.

What's next? A lingering shower is possible early Sunday before skies gradually clear and highs reach the mid-80s. A nicer, less humid start to the workweek.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: The chance for isolated to scattered showers and a storm rises this evening. Scattered showers and storms are likely overnight, when a few downpours could produce flooding, especially in urban areas. Patchy fog is possible after midnight, too. Muggy with lows near 70 to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow (Sunday): A leftover shower or storm is possible early in the morning, then skies gradually clear as afternoon sun builds. Highs should get to within a few degrees of 85 with elevated dew points still keeping it muggy. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Partly to mostly clear as humidity begins to slowly decrease. A stray shower is slightly possible. Lows in the mid-60s to low 70s Confidence: Medium

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Nicer to start the workweek, with highs Monday and Tuesday in the upper 70s to low 80s, and dew points falling from the 60s into the 50s. Skies are generally partly to mostly sunny as high pressure gradually builds in, though a passing shower can't be totally ruled out Monday. Confidence: Medium

Temperatures and humidity creep up Wednesday and Thursday. Highs in the low to mid-80s Wednesday reach the mid- to upper 80s Thursday, while dew points climb back well into the 60s. It should be generally dry other than a shower possible late Thursday. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Mostly cloudy and muggy today, rain tonight. Meh. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for September 12

An intense 1934 cloudburst dumped over 4 inches of rain—most of it in a single hour—turning streets into rivers and overwhelming infrastructure across the city.
